seo.og_title: Dakhla Travel Guide | Sahara meets the Atlantic – Lagoon, Kitesurf & Desert
seo.og_description: Discover Dakhla, nicknamed the Sahara meets the Atlantic: intact turquoise lagoon, authentic oyster farms, kitesurf camps, itinerary and day trips in one guide.

name: Dakhla
hero_subtitle: Where the Sahara meets the Atlantic: a 40 km turquoise lagoon, world-class kitesurf winds, the White Dune and Dragon Island.

overview.title: Welcome to Dakhla — lagoon, wind and desert shore
overview.p1: Dakhla sits on a long sand peninsula in Morocco’s far south, where Saharan dunes meet a vast Atlantic lagoon. The town is modest; the landscape is the destination — flat turquoise water, steady trade winds, and landmarks like the White Dune and Dragon Island that feel almost unreal.
overview.p2: Riders come for kitesurf and wingfoil on glass-smooth shallows. Everyone else comes for boat trips on the lagoon, oyster tastings, desert tracks and relaxing evenings by the bay. Allow three to five days if you want both wind sports and slow exploration.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Dakhla
places.subtitle: Lagoon, White Dune, Dragon Island, wind spots and the working port.

lagune.title: Dakhla Lagoon
lagune.desc: A 40 km turquoise lagoon between the Sahara and the Atlantic — the heart of Dakhla and a world kitesurf stage.

dune_blanche.title: White Dune (Dune Blanche)
dune_blanche.desc: A pure white sand dune rising from the lagoon; at high tide it sits in turquoise water like an island.

ile_dragon.title: Dragon Island
ile_dragon.desc: A rocky islet in the lagoon whose silhouette looks like a sleeping dragon; boat or low-tide access.

kitesurf.title: Kitesurf & Wingfoil Spots
kitesurf.desc: Flat water, steady trade winds and camps along the lagoon for beginners and advanced riders.

port.title: Fishing Port & Corniche
port.desc: Working harbour, evening promenade and the everyday face of the peninsula town.

sources_asnaa.title: Asnaa Hot Springs
sources_asnaa.desc: Natural warm sulfur pools inland from the lagoon — a quiet contrast after wind and sand.

foum_el_bouir.title: Foum El Bouir (Ocean Side)
foum_el_bouir.desc: Atlantic wave spot on the ocean side of the peninsula for surf and advanced sessions.

huitres.title: Oyster Farms
huitres.desc: Lagoon oyster farms with tastings — a simple, local way to taste the fresh harvest of the bay.

imlili.title: Imlili Sebkha & Pools
imlili.desc: Inland desert depressions featuring small natural water pools and tiny fish in the heart of the arid landscape.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Lagoon orientation, signature landscapes, then wind or ocean.

day1.title: Town & lagoon
day1.desc: Walk the harbour and seafront to get your bearings in the peninsula town.

day2.title: Signature landscapes
day2.desc: 4x4 or organised access to the white sand landmark and dragon-shaped islet.

day3.title: Wind or ocean
day3.desc: Lagoon school session for beginners, or ocean waves at Foum El Bouir.

directory.title: Find Your Ideal Stay in Dakhla
directory.subtitle: Lagoon camps, hotels in town and stays near the kite spots.
directory.no_results: No accommodations match this filter combination. Try broadening your search.

eat.title: Where to Eat in Dakhla
eat.subtitle: Fresh fish, lagoon oysters and local seafood tables.

oyster_farm.title: The Oyster Farm (Ferme Oycéenne)
oyster_farm.desc: Taste freshly harvested oysters straight from the bay, paired with grilled fish and lemon right by the water.

asmaa.title: Restaurant Asmaa
asmaa.desc: Renowned for serving the absolute best catch of the day, royal shrimps and exquisite fish tagines in town.

talmoukt.title: Talmoukt
talmoukt.desc: A favorite among locals and travelers for hearty Moroccan dishes, friendly service, and perfectly grilled local fish.

ocean_vagabond.title: Ocean Vagabond Beach Restaurant
ocean_vagabond.desc: Relaxed open-air dining right on the lagoon shore, serving healthy bowls, fresh seafood, wood-fired pizzas and cocktails.

westpoint_rest.title: Westpoint Restaurant
westpoint_rest.desc: Overlooking the Atlantic waves, offering a refined menu blending international dishes, local fish and soothing sunset views.

casa_jose.title: Casa Jose
casa_jose.desc: Popular spot known for Spanish-inspired seafood tapas, paella, and warm hospitality in the heart of town.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.desc: Inside town, yellow "Petit Taxis" are easy to find. For reaching the lagoon camps or White Dune, 4x4 rentals or camp shuttles are recommended.

bargain.title: Local Souks
bargain.desc: Explore the central municipal market for local crafts, Saharan spices, and silver jewelry with friendly and relaxed negotiations.

water.title: Stay Hydrated
water.desc: The desert climate can be deceptively breezy. Drink bottled water regularly and enjoy fresh local juices during your stay.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Dakhla
daytrips.subtitle: Signature lagoon loops and longer desert tracks.

dune_trip.title: White Dune & lagoon loop
dune_trip.desc: Half-day 4x4 or boat outing combining the White Dune and lagoon viewpoints.

imlili_trip.title: Imlili sebkha
imlili_trip.desc: Salt flats and natural desert pools south of Dakhla — a full-day track with a local driver.

ocean_beaches.title: Ocean-side beaches
ocean_beaches.desc: Foum El Bouir and wild Atlantic stretches for surf and empty sand.

tropic_cancer.title: Tropic of Cancer marker
tropic_cancer.desc: A symbolic stop on the peninsula road — quick photo and sense of latitude.

q1.question: How many days do I need in Dakhla?
q1.answer: Three days cover the lagoon highlights and one excursion. Five days suit kitesurf progress plus White Dune and Dragon Island at a relaxed pace.

q2.question: Is Dakhla only for kitesurfers?
q2.answer: No. The lagoon, White Dune, Dragon Island, oyster farms and desert tracks work for non-riders. Wind sports are the main draw, not the only one.

q3.question: How do I get to Dakhla?
q3.answer: Dakhla has a domestic airport (VIL) with flights from major Moroccan cities like Casablanca and Marrakech. Overland, it is a scenic coastal drive from the north.

q4.question: When is the best time to visit?
q4.answer: For wind sports, spring through early autumn brings the steadiest trade winds. Winter is milder for sightseeing and can still offer great sessions.

detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Fresh fish and a quiet end to the first day.

detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Boat or tide-dependent approach to the dragon-shaped islet.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Return for a simple dinner and early night if you ride the next day.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Kitesurf lesson or free ride
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Lagoon school session for beginners, or open water for experienced riders.
detailed_itinerary.day3_a: Afternoon — Foum El Bouir or oysters
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Ocean-side waves or a lagoon oyster tasting, depending on energy and wind.
